basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Health information about one person across sources, not a provider's operational record.
Each assertion keeps its kind, time and source, so self-reported and clinician-recorded data stay distinct.
Consent, access and correction are part of the record.
Differs from population health data, which is aggregated.

may: Help the person collect and organize their own health records.
Summarize records with their sources and dates.
Remind the person of plans, medications and appointments they recorded.
Flag inconsistencies such as duplicate medications for review.
mustNot: Share records without the person's consent or a lawful basis.
Alter clinical entries; corrections go through the source.
Use health data for advertising, insurance pricing or employment decisions.
Hide uncertainty or the age of data.

considerations: Health data is among the most sensitive personal data.
People have a right to access and correct their records.
Errors can lead to dangerous treatment decisions.
Stigma can follow disclosure of mental health, sexual health or genetic data.

items: A personal health record is tied to one person and holds dated assertions with source and kind.
It is confused with a provider's electronic health record and with fitness app data.
Outdated allergy or medication lists causing harm.
Misreading self-reported data as clinical findings.
IHE profiles for cross-enterprise document sharing (XDS).
ISO/TS 22220 for subject of care identification.
